name: init
why: PID 1 on every Unix; Debian ships it as sysvinit-core's /sbin/init, which no daemon rule picks up

name: launchd
why: macOS PID 1: it has no plist of its own in /System/Library/LaunchDaemons

name: runit
why: init and supervision suite; Debian's runit package ships no daemon-tagged or service-unit binary named runit

name: postgres
why: PostgreSQL's server process; Debian installs it under usr/lib/postgresql/<version>/bin, outside every program rule

name: s6-svscan
why: the s6 supervision tree's root daemon (skarnet s6)

name: upstart
why: Ubuntu's init from 2006 to 2014; no longer packaged

name: lpsched
why: the System V / Solaris print service scheduler

name: pdflush
why: Linux 2.6.0 to 2.6.31 writeback kernel thread, replaced by per-bdi flusher threads

name: bdflush
why: Linux 2.4 buffer-flush kernel daemon, before pdflush

name: kupdated
why: Linux 2.4 kernel thread that flushed old dirty buffers

name: update
why: the historical Unix daemon that called sync(2) every 30 seconds (V7 to 4.4BSD update(8))
